A seller's contact point is written as a person's name, never as a department's.
The buyer's contact is not written: a report that names one is refused as `unknown-property`.

That KoSIT raises no warning of a contact's telephone number or email address in a file report-spec takes rests on report-spec's tests and the e-invoice gate's holding of XRechnung's expressions and the tests that read them: the one file the gate judges in KoSIT's XRechnung scenario is 0038's sample, whose contact is the addressed sample's, and no sample's page prints the business process, the seller's address or the contact, the XRechnung sample's printing only the buyer's Leitweg-ID.

report-spec's `xrechnung.ts` holds two expressions copied as strings from KoSIT's XRechnung schematron, whose licence was not read; whether copying them is acceptable under 0006 is the rightsholder's question.
A report whose e-invoice is an XRechnung is refused whole by 0.2.0, as `unknown-kind`, so a report saved with one opens only in a release that has it.

The resolved document's e-invoice names its kind, so a renderer of this release refuses a Factur-X file without one, as an e-invoice of a kind it does not know, and a document a host builds by hand names it.
An XRechnung is version 3.0 of XRechnung's standard, written as CII alone, so a buyer or an access point that asks for UBL, XRechnung 4.0, its extension or CVD, or a credit note cannot be served.

An XRechnung needs a business process, a buyer's reference, payment instructions, the seller's contact of all three terms and both parties' electronic addresses, each refused where it is missing or, written or read from data, blank, so a seller with no telephone number to give cannot issue one.

An XRechnung's payment terms may hold no line that begins with #, a well-formed Skonto line of XRechnung's own syntax among them, so a discount for early payment is said in words no buyer's system reads until XRechnung 4.0.

An electronic address under 0204 is held to a Leitweg-ID's shape and check digits in an e-invoice of either kind, a shape read from FeRD's description and secondary sources, since the format specification could not be read on 21 October 2026, and checked against KoSIT's test values alone, so an address the specification allows and this shape does not is refused, and three Leitweg-IDs of KoSIT's own test suite, of wrong check digits, are.
An XRechnung's buyer's reference is held to no Leitweg-ID's form, and nothing here knows whether a Leitweg-ID belongs to a buyer, routes an invoice, or is taken by a portal.

An XRechnung's PDF is a plain copy, no PDF/A and no embedded file, every page headed by the runtime's English label that it is not the invoice, so a host that sends the PDF alone sends no invoice, and the label is all that says so.

The renderer refuses an XRechnung whose page header does not open with the copy's label as the runtime writes it, its paragraph's style and all, or whose syntax, version or guideline is not report-spec's, so a document a host builds otherwise than the runtime resolves it is refused.

KoSIT's XRechnung scenario and Mustang judge one XRechnung, the corpus's sample, and four controls of it, Mustang firing 25 rules on it against 179 of FeRD's on a Factur-X sample in the run recorded on 21 October 2026, so a customer's XRechnung is held by report-spec's rules and by the rules of XRechnung's schematron the gate names, and not by a validator; the gate ran on Windows alone, on 21 October 2026, never in CI.
That XRechnung 3.0 stays in force until any date rests on a secondary source: KoSIT's own "Versionen und Bundles" page was not read.

XRechnung's specification identifier, the contexts and tests the e-invoice gate holds its rules to, and the sample's Leitweg-ID are copied from KoSIT's configuration and test suite, whose licences were not read, and whether that is acceptable under 0006, as whether the sample's title may name XRechnung, is the rightsholder's question.

A QR-bill's fields edit its texts run by run and add or remove nothing else: a run added to or removed from a text, a literal run made a binding or a binding a literal, and a reference's type, which is read from its text, have no field, and a debtor bound to the data, removed and added again, comes back as SIX's example in literal text, bound again only by undo.

A QR-bill added from nothing is SIX's third example -- its IBAN and its sample foundation of Bern as the creditor -- and is warned of until its account is none of SIX's examples and its creditor no longer SIX's sample foundation, which is not to say either is the creditor's; the builders ask for no account first.

A bill that holds, written in the report, one of SIX's four example accounts, or the creditor, the debtor or the QR reference a builder puts in from SIX's examples, is warned of once as `example-payment-part`, the invoice starter and its samples among them, which pay an example account on purpose and so open with that warning; a text read from the data, an account that pays no creditor for another reason, another of SIX's example parties or references typed by hand, and an example party with one part changed are not warned of.
The warning that a bill holds SIX's examples is listed among the problems, on the bill, and drawn on no field -- the IBAN's among them -- which a builder would mark invalid.

A changed IBAN is checked by SIX's rules -- country, length, check digits and a QR-IBAN's currency -- and confirmed by nothing: a valid account of someone else's, typed or pasted, is taken, so who may change whom a bill pays is the host's, through who it lets edit the report, and a proposal's review that shows such a change above every other, comparing the bill whole where a proposal replaces the document, is not built.

An IBAN of the other kind than the bill's reference changes the reference in the same step: a QR-IBAN typed over a creditor reference or none gives the bill SIX's example QR reference, and an IBAN typed over a QR reference removes it, so what was in the reference is gone until undo, which the live region says rather than asks. A reference read from the data is left as it is, and a QR-IBAN in a bill in euro is refused until the currency is francs.

In a report with an e-invoice the QR-bill's IBAN is the e-invoice's account (BT-84): typed into the bill it changes the e-invoice's and every EPC QR code's too, in one step (0044), and one the e-invoice or a code cannot take is refused on the bill's field.

Every report without a QR-bill offers Add QR-bill in its own properties, a report that cannot take one among them -- a Letter or landscape page, an e-invoice that names no account or one a bill cannot pay -- where pressing it is refused in report-spec's words.
`Selection` is a component, a table's column or a part of the report's own level, so a host's code that read `selection.id` narrows it to a `ComponentSelection` first.
A text that prints "Payment part" names its outline row and its box as a QR-bill's row and band are named, so the two cannot be told apart by name.
The Studio's Preview offers no "Select …" for a runtime refusal of a QR-bill, which names no component.

report-builder.css is an entry that imports its rules from files of `styles/`, which the package publishes beside it: a bundler inlines them, a page that links the entry as it stands asks the browser for each of them, and a host that copies the entry by hand copies `styles/` too.

That a bill's code pays the IBAN typed is held by the browser gate, in CI and on a developer's machine: the PDF the Studio offers in Chromium is drawn by PDF.js and its code decoded by ZXing in the gate's own Node process, never by a banking app, as 0022 says of every bill.

A font is read by report-spec's `readFont` as one static TrueType file, so a collection, a WOFF or WOFF2 web font, an EOT, a Type 1 font, a CFF-flavoured OpenType font (.otf) and a variable font are each refused, and a host converts or obtains a TrueType file of each face before it approves one.

A font whose OS/2 fsType says Restricted License, No subsetting or Bitmap embedding only is refused with no override, even where its vendor grants embedding by contract, and one that says Installable may still be under a licence that forbids generating documents with it, which nothing here reads: the licence description `readFont` hands back is the customer's to read.
A colour font, one with COLR, SVG, CBDT or sbix glyphs, is refused even where its outlines would print in one colour.
A font mapped only in the Windows symbol encoding or a legacy one is refused, as ten of the 447 font files of one Windows machine measured on 21 and 22 October 2026 were.
A font past 20 MB and one with a glyph whose points times its contours pass 1,048,576 are refused, as SimSun-ExtB, 21.9 MB, was of that machine's fonts.
A font that maps more than 131,072 characters is refused.

A font whose horizontal header puts its ascender at or below the baseline or its descender above it, or makes a line shorter than half its em or taller than four, is refused as malformed, since pdfmake lays every line of it out by that line; none of the 425 fonts measured on one machine on 22 October 2026 was.

A font is read as fontkit, which PDFKit prints with, reads it, not only as the OpenType specification asks: a table recorded as empty is refused, and a PostScript name in an encoding fontkit decodes otherwise than report-spec's reader, or a naming table fontkit could not decode, is refused, where another reader might take the font.

`characterMap` reads a font's character map alone, whatever length the directory records for it, and holds no glyph to the font's glyph count, so the characters a host's font is held to are `readFont`'s, which holds both.

That fontkit, which PDFKit lays text out and subsets with, maps, names and draws a font as report-spec's reader says and embeds what it accepts is held on Roboto 3.014, Liberation Sans 2.1.5, every recorded length of two of their faces' tables and 160 corruptions of the same two, and not on a customer's font; and the layout tables fontkit runs at print, GSUB, GPOS, kern and morx, are not read, so a crafted one can fail a render with an error rather than a refusal, or never let it end: a morx table of one state that never advances, in a font the reader accepts, kept PDFKit laying one letter out until it was stopped after 20 seconds, on 22 October 2026.

A data source is held to the syntax of identifiers, so a submission's id other than letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-', at most 128 characters and starting with a letter or a digit, one holding a space, an '@', a '/', a ':' or a letter beyond ASCII among them, is refused, and a host whose ids hold anything else maps them to ids that fit or names no source.

A source's identifiers are held by their syntax and not their meaning, so a host that names its submissions by a single-word name, a personal number such as an AHV number, an IBAN or a file name, or a version's hash by any 64 hex digits, the SHA-256 of an email address among them, passes the check and puts that value in every manifest.
The runtime holds a source's form and not its truth, so a source a host writes by hand reaches the manifest as written.

The manifest of data read from Formancy Data names the published forms each dataset was read from, and neither the record a report printed nor which publication of each form answered, which Data 0.5.0 does not say.

A manifest names every submission its data came from, with its form's id and its version's hash, so one of 100,000 submissions with UUIDs was 14,400,305 bytes of JSON, and 35,400,305 with ids and form ids of 128 characters, and checking its source added a median of about 170 ms to checking the rows, measured on one machine on 21 October 2026.

A source names no more submissions than the data gives detail rows, or one where it gives none, so a host that reads several submissions into one row, or names submissions whose rows it left out, is refused, and names the submissions it printed or no source.

The Data provider refuses, as `unexpected-form` and before any record is read, a form a server answers under another id than the one the binding names, which 0.2.0's provider read; Data 0.5.0 answers a form under its own id.
A manifest holds no digest of the data, no time of its capture and no version of its provider, so it says where the data came from and cannot show that what printed is what was captured.
Data that names a source is refused by 0.2.0's runtime as `unknown-property`, so a host that names one, or uses this release's Data provider, needs this release's runtime.
A report whose dataset is read from a formancy form is refused whole by 0.2.0, as `unknown-property`, so a report saved with that binding opens only in a release that has it.

The form bridge fetches nothing, so a host prints a submission against the version that collected it only if it kept that version's document or fetches it from a formancy server of 0.8.0 or later, which serves each version's document by its number; 0.7.0's served its current version's alone.
A default a spec 5 form gives a field, left alone by the person filling it in, is stored by formancy as their answer, indistinguishable from one they chose, and prints as one.

The form bridge never matches an answer against its field's `pattern`, so an answer the pattern refuses, in a submission formancy's engine never stored, prints; and a version whose pattern can be made to backtrack, which formancy published before 0.12.0, is read and printed like any other.

A formancy time of day prints as stored, at the width its field's spec 6 `precision` gives, so the submissions of a form version that gives it a precision print its seconds and their digits, `09:50:12.250`, beside an earlier version's `09:50`; an answer at another width than its own version's is refused as `invalid-answer`.

A formancy `number` answer whose double's shortest decimal has more than 15 significant digits, a total the form computed among them, one past 2^53, whichever field reads it, or one with a fraction read into an integer field, is refused as `inexact-number` and never rounded; a form that must print such a number holds it as text under a decimal pattern, as Formancy Data writes one, which a report reads as a decimal.

A number typed with more than 15 significant digits was rounded when formancy stored it as a double, and prints as that double's shortest decimal where that has at most 15 digits, so a typed 0.10000000000000001 prints 0.1.
An integer field over a formancy number whose version steps through fractions, by its step or from a fractional least value, is refused for every submission of that version, whatever its answers.

A submission paired with another version than the one that collected it is refused only where one of its answers has no field in that version, so two versions with the same paths and other labels print the labels of the version the host handed over.

A version that removed, moved or retyped a field a report reads refuses every submission of that version, naming the field, the version's hash and the review, which offers what would lift it where anything does, until a review's resolution is applied or the report is changed by hand.

A field read from a group's child, a matrix row or an option has the id its report gives it, never one made from its path, so where two paths would flatten to one name the author names them apart, and nothing renames a field by similarity.
An answer formancy pruned from a hidden field, or that was never given, is handed over as null, so a field declared not nullable refuses a final render of any submission that left it out.

Labels print from the version's catalogue for the locale a render prints in, the report's own unless the render names a translation's (0063), or from its default catalogue where it has none for that locale, formancy's own fallback, so a report in de-CH of a form with only German and English catalogues prints its default's labels.
A choice whose options a deployment resolves prints only the labels the host's resolver gives, and a submission is refused as `unresolved-label` where it gives no string or throws.

A select or a radio that offers no options in the document and names no source takes any non-empty string, as formancy's engine takes from 0.8.0, so its stored value prints unchecked with `read: 'value'`, its label is refused, and an empty string is refused as `invalid-answer`, as for any choice.
A file, a signature, a ranking and ticked boxes whose options a deployment resolves are refused as `unsupported-field`, never printed as something else.
A yes-or-no radio of "true" and "false", as Formancy Data writes one, prints its label or its value as text, and is refused where a report reads it as a boolean.
A repeater row formancy nulled when it stripped it is refused in any repeater the submission holds, whether the report reads that repeater or not, so such a submission does not print.
A rich text answer whose markup is longer than the runtime's 16,384 characters is refused before formancy's parser reads it, however short its words.
A report of one row per submission is refused for a list of no submissions, since its source names each submission it was read from.
A report reads one repeater of a form as its detail, and a form's other repeaters cannot be expressed in this version of the format.

Reading one submission of 100,000 repeater rows of six fields took a median of 966 ms, and 100,000 submissions of eleven fields, one a row, 2,135 ms, from the built package on an Intel i9-10900K under Node 24.21.0 at about a tenth of its load from other work, on 22 October 2026, before the runtime checks the data again when it resolves.

A report prints its sans, serif and mono text in fonts a host approved, mapped to its three tokens and pinned by digest; a token a report leaves unmapped prints in the renderer's own face, so serif and mono print nothing until a report maps them, exactly as before 0.3.0.

A host's font is the customer's to license: its OS/2 fsType is a vendor's hint the runtime and the renderer honour, so a font that says Installable may still be under an agreement that forbids a server generating documents with it, which nothing here reads, and 0006's guard, which reads the fonts a published package ships, never sees it.

A character a mapped face has no glyph for is refused, naming the face and the code point, never drawn in another face: there is no fallback across the three families, and a report that needs a character its font lacks maps a font that has it.

Latin, Greek and Cyrillic, with the punctuation, symbols and marks written with them, are the scripts a report prints, by an allowlist of Unicode blocks: every other script is refused by code point in any face, Roboto's included -- the right-to-left, shaping and CJK scripts, and simple alphabets such as Armenian, Georgian and Coptic -- until a fixture proves it, and so are the bidirectional controls, since pdfmake lays out no bidirectional text and the renderer runs no shaping.

A font whose outlines hold more points, more points times contours or more composite components together than report-spec's MAX_FONT_POINTS, MAX_FONT_OUTLINE_WORK and MAX_FONT_COMPONENTS allow is refused as too large, so that subsetting it cannot hold a render for minutes; the bounds sit just past the largest TrueType fonts measured, which are Hangul and Han fonts no report prints in.

A CFF-flavoured OpenType font (`.otf`) is refused, as 0040 refuses one, because report-spec's reader reads no CFF outlines, so the renderer cannot hold one to its rules, though veraPDF accepted a PDF/A-3b PDFKit drew in one; a TrueType file (`.ttf`) of each face is mapped instead, until a later release reads CFF outlines and the e-invoice gate proves a CFF face.

A host face's layout tables -- GSUB, GPOS, GDEF, kern and the AAT morx state machine -- are stripped before it is embedded, so that a crafted one can neither hang nor crash a render, and its ligatures, kerning and contextual shaping are lost, combining marks placed by their boxes; the Latin, Greek and Cyrillic a report prints needs none of them. A face of the very bytes of the renderer's own Roboto or Liberation Sans keeps them, since PDFKit draws it and the renderer's own as one. The list was read from fontkit 2.0.4, which a test pins.

Every render reads each face it maps again, under a millisecond for a typical font, and holds it twice until the render ends, the runtime's copy and the stripped one; nothing of a face is kept from one render to the next, and two renders at once write their faces into pdfmake's process-wide virtual files under names of their own, which each pass removes.

Each line counts toward the page limit by the face it prints in, so a report set in a host face of a short line passes the bound that refuses it before layout with up to 2.3 times the lines Roboto's would, at a face's shortest line of half its size, and pdfmake measures them all before its page limit refuses what does not fit; text in Roboto beside such a face is bounded as before.

A host face is refused as an invalid asset where any of its PostScript names is another face's of the render with other bytes -- another host asset's, or the renderer's own Roboto's or Liberation Sans's, whether or not the report prints in it -- or is `null` or a name every JavaScript object has, since PDFKit draws two faces of one name as whichever it opened first: a host's own Roboto or Liberation Sans of another release than the renderer's is refused, and a family whose two faces state one name, while the renderer's own bytes of either are accepted.

A document handed to the renderer with text set outside the format's 4 to 96 pt is refused, as report-spec's validator refuses such a report, since the page bound counts each line by its size; a document the runtime resolved never holds one.

Which face a run printed in is read back from the PDF by its PostScript name, on Liberation Serif and Mono printing Latin, Greek and Cyrillic; the corpus's text box still assumes a descent of a fifth of the font size, so those faces are chosen for descenders that reach about that far, and a host face with a deeper descender is not proved against the overlap checks.

A report that maps a font is refused by 0.2.0's validator as an unknown property, and its runtime and renderer must be of one release: a 0.2.0 renderer handed this runtime's document prints a mapped sans in Roboto without a word. No serif or mono face is shipped: the Liberation Sans a package ships is for the QR-bill slip and the EPC caption alone.

An e-invoice is edited and never made from nothing in the builders: a report becomes one through the host, a paste or the Studio's e-invoice starter, and the editor's `addPart` of one is refused as `unavailable`.

The account an e-invoice shares with its QR-bill and its EPC QR codes is changed by one command, `setPaymentAccount`, which changes no BIC, so an EPC QR code whose BIC is of another country refuses the new account until its BIC is changed or emptied, an account outside the EEA, which needs a BIC, cannot follow one inside it in one edit, and a report with a QR-bill keeps a Swiss or Liechtenstein account.
Where the e-invoice, its QR-bill or an EPC QR code reads its account from the data, `setPaymentAccount` refuses as `read-from-data`, naming the place, rather than write over the binding.

Where any of the e-invoice, its QR-bill and its EPC QR codes reads its account from the data, a builder's IBAN field writes its own place's account alone, which the render compares with the data's, and where two others are written, one changed alone is refused until the person binds them alike or writes the third.

report-core holds an e-invoice's totals and its lines to the page and no other term, so the seller's name, address or VAT identifier, the issue or due date, the BIC or the account's name, changed in a builder, is accepted with no warning where the page prints it in its own words, as the e-invoice starter does, and the XML then says another thing than the page, which § 14c UStG may count as a second invoice: the person changes both.

In a report with an e-invoice the palette's EPC payment code pays the e-invoice's account with its BIC and is unavailable until the e-invoice gives payment instructions, and Add QR-bill gives the bill the e-invoice's currency and account, so it is refused where that account is not one of Switzerland or Liechtenstein.

What a template prints beside an e-invoice's totals in its own words, as the e-invoice starter's "Umsatzsteuer 19 % auf" and its "IBAN:" line do, is not changed when the e-invoice's rate or account is, so an author changes both.

A seller's contact, payment instructions and an exempt or reverse-charged VAT category added in a builder hold the editor's placeholder words and values, which reach nobody and are written into the XML until a person replaces them, with no warning, and an exempt category's reason names no provision, which § 14 Abs. 4 Satz 1 Nr. 8 UStG asks for.
An e-invoice's properties are one long pane of fields in groups that scrolls, which no gate measures, and their German and French words have not been read by a native speaker.

report-builder-core's `PropertyGroup` holds a list of buttons, `actions`, each with `available` and `then`, where 0039's unreleased `action` was one, and `REPORT_LEVEL_PARTS` holds `eInvoice`, so a host's code that read one button or took the bill for the only part changes with this release.
report-core refuses with a new code, `read-from-data`, so a host that maps every refusal code to its own message meets one it has no message for.

The browser gate holds the shared account on the e-invoice starter's XML and its EPC QR code, decoded from the PDF's pixels, and the starter has no QR-bill, so the bill's half is held by the builder scenarios in jsdom and not on a PDF.

A report generated from a formancy form is a first draft -- a line for each answer under the form's own title, whatever the report's language, sections with no space between them and every column of its table as wide as the next -- which nobody would print as it is, and which an author makes the report.

A generated report is in the form's model order and follows none of the layouts the form names, so a print layout that leaves a field out, or orders the fields otherwise, is not what the draft prints.
A tick box or a ticked option in a generated report prints `[x]` or `[ ]`, in no language, and an unanswered one as nothing.

A form whose generated report would declare more than 64 fields or hold more components than a region holds, that heads a column with a label longer than 200 characters, labels anything with a control character or nests a field past 16 keys, gives no report at all: it is refused, and nothing picks the fields to keep.

A generated report's table of more than six columns stands on a landscape page, and one of more than nine gives no report at all -- the site visit form read one row per submission, thirteen columns, among them -- since every column is as wide as the next and needs 80 pt for a heading's word.

A generated report whose heading or answer holds a word wider than its column -- `Zusammenfassung`, 77.8 pt, wider than the 72 pt a column of a full page holds -- or a label in characters Roboto has no glyph for, such as Chinese or an emoji, is generated, and refused by the renderer when it prints: the generator holds no font to see it.

A field labelled longer than 200 characters in a form prints its label whole on its line in a generated report, and is labelled in the report's data by its row's or option's label, or by its key, with a note saying so.

A field of a generated report is nullable unless the version requires it and no visible or skip rule can hide it, so an expression over most form fields reads a member that may be null, which CEL types as dyn.

Where any row or option of a matrix or of ticked boxes has a value that is no field key, every member of that field takes its place among its kind's as its id in a generated report, `checks_2`, so an expression names it by place, and a later version that moves the option moves what that id would mean.

No generated base is kept beside a report, so nothing regenerates a report from a later form version: a review offers its new labels for the texts that say an old one and says its new fields, and applies neither.
A generated report takes one repeater as its table, the one asked for, and lists the others as left out, so a form with two lists prints one.

That a generated report opens with no warning in the editor is held by report-core's diagnose on the Studio's site visit starter alone; every other generated report is held to the runtime's checkReport, which refuses errors and passes warnings.

Generating the site visit took 1.8 to 3.9 ms, refusing a form of 100,000 fields 2.3 to 5.2 s, most of it formancy's validator, and refusing a grid of 100,000 columns 0.89 to 3.1 s, from the built package on an Intel i9-10900K under Node 24.21.0 at 3 to 100 % of its load from other work, on 22 October 2026.

The server answers GET /health, GET /v1/whoami and the routes later records add, a template’s draft and its images since 0049, and nothing else: no publication, render job or artifact exists in this release, and every other method and path is answered 404.

A path with anything a proxy could normalise, an escape, a dot or an empty segment, a trailing slash or / alone among them, is answered 400 path-not-plain before any route, so a client that adds a trailing slash or escapes a character no name needs escaped is refused.
A request that takes longer than 300 seconds to arrive, Node’s own default, which Fastify turns off and nothing here measured, has its connection closed.

Every token must carry the claim FORMANCY_REPORT_ATTRIBUTES names as its tenant, so a single-tenant host puts a constant in every token, and a token without it is refused with the same 401 as a forgery.
A token is trusted until its exp: the server keeps no session and asks the host nothing, so a person removed at the host keeps their token’s access until it expires.
The actions table names the actions of R14 before the routes that take them, so whoami lists the version and policy actions no route answers yet, and a later release may change a row.

The audit trail names who asked only by a keyed hash under FORMANCY_REPORT_AUDIT_KEY, and nobody without one, so an operator finds a person’s events by computing the reference, where Formancy Data’s trail names its actor plainly.

The audit trail is operational, not evidence: written to the server’s log by the same process after the answer, so an event can be lost, and a request no route answered, a 404 or a path that does not decode, writes none.
A FORMANCY_REPORT_ variable the server does not read stops it at start, naming it, so a setting of a later release cannot be set before that release runs.

A list of trusted proxies is refused only when its entries together trust every IPv4 or every IPv6 peer as @fastify/proxy-addr 5.1.2 matches one, so a list that trusts half of IPv4 starts, and so does ::/1, which holds the IPv4-mapped range and which that matcher compares with no IPv4 peer.
The server is one instance: its rate limit is counted in its own memory and starts again with it, and two instances behind one address are not a supported deployment.
HEAD is answered on /health alone, so a client that probes the API with HEAD is answered 404.
The server’s image builds and runs on Node 26, at the digest packages/report-server/Dockerfile pins in both of its stages, while the packages run on Node 22.13 or later.
This release publishes no server image: an operator builds it from the repository with packages/report-server/Dockerfile.

The image’s operating system layer, Alpine Linux with BusyBox under GPL-2.0 among its packages, is not read by the dependency licence guard, which reads npm packages, and no record yet says how it is read.

The server depends on Formancy Data’s @formancy/data-identity, under Data’s source-available licence, so running it in production needs a production licence for Formancy Data as well as for Report, even beside no Data server.

The server verifies tokens under exactly Data 0.5.0’s rules, through its verifier at that version, so a rule Data changes later reaches Report only through a release of report-server that moves the pin.
The verifier tolerates 30 seconds of clock skew on exp and nbf, data-identity’s default, which the server does not change and nothing here measured.

A token that is not exactly its compact form, a signature with = after it or a space in it among them, is refused with the one 401, as Data’s server refuses it since 0.4.0, so a host whose library pads a token’s parts is refused.

A form version that removed, moved or retyped a field a report reads refuses every submission of it until someone applies a resolution of its review: nothing is followed by itself, a rename the form's author declared included.

A review needs every version the report names -- the one it was made from and each its overrides name -- handed over beside the new one, and is refused as `missing-version` without one, so a host that did not keep a version cannot review against it.

A followed rename keeps reading where it read each version the host handed the review over; a version it kept and did not hand over, which printed at the old path, is refused once the binding moves, until its own review offers the path the version the report was made from reads.
A field a version removed blocks every later version that lacks it too, each reviewed in turn, since printing nothing of it names one version; or the field is removed from the report.

A field moved without a declared rename is offered nothing but printing nothing of it from that version, another type or its removal, or the path a version the report names reads where formancy's diff finds the same field: a path is never guessed from a name, so the author moves the binding by hand.
A field renamed and retyped in the same version is offered no rename, since following it alone would still refuse that version's submissions.

A field the QR-bill or the e-invoice reads, directly or through an aggregate, is offered only a rename by its review: printing nothing of it, another type or its removal would change what the bill or the invoice says, so a version that removed one blocks until the part is changed by its own commands.

A version that removed the detail's repeater, or holds another kind there, is offered nothing but a rename of it, declared or read so by a version the report names; printing none of its rows, or removing the detail, is the author's to do.

Printing nothing of a field from a version declares the field nullable, which an expression reads as dyn; where that would leave an expression the compiler refuses, a decimal compared with `==` among them, it is not offered.

A retype is judged by the fields' kinds, never by the answers: a version that holds the field as text, retyped to a number, has each of its submissions whose answer spells no number refused as `invalid-answer`, which the resolution says of that version and cannot say of a submission.

A key a version removed a field from, never reviewed, and a later version reused for another field, prints that field's answers as the report's; a review says so only against a version the report names that printed nothing of the field there.

A relabel is offered only for a text that says a label of a version the report names, word for word -- the field's own label, a line's label run before the run that prints it, or a column's heading over it -- so a label reworded, inside a sentence, given by a version the report never named, or a matrix row's or option's composite label is not found, and one the format cannot hold, past `MAX_LABEL_LENGTH`, or holding a direction control or a separator, is not offered.
A field a version adds is said by its review and never added; an option or a matrix row a version adds to a field the report reads is not said.

A version that no longer requires a field the report declares never null, or that hides it by a rule, blocks nothing and is not said by its review: a final render of a submission that left the field out is refused as `unexpected-null`.
A version that names its form by another id is said by its review and blocks nothing: the per-render check reads a field of any form wherever it stands where the report reads it.

Removing a field with its readers removes every component, column, style rule, footer cell, sort key, group and aggregate that reads it, a footer row left with no cell, a table left with no column and a section whose condition reads it with all they hold, and refuses a field the QR-bill or the e-invoice reads, as `read-by-part`.

A report whose binding names an override for a form version is refused whole by 0.2.0, as `unknown-property`, and a field or the detail holds at most 64 of them, a followed rename naming each version handed over that read the old path; past that no rename is offered.
A batch holds at most 1,000 commands, chosen, refused past it before any of it runs, and no batch inside it; a step that throws on what the steps before it left is refused, the batch with it.

Reviewing the site visit starter against its version 3 took 7 to 11 ms, a draft of 64 fields against a version that removed or renamed every one 75 to 118 ms, and a batch of 1,000 commands applied and undone 2 to 3 ms; a report at the format's bounds, 2,500 components each reading ten of 64 header fields, against a version that removed every field, 6.4 to 6.6 s where every field may be null and 49 to 50 s where none may, each nothing printed then compiled over the expressions its field reaches: from the built packages on an Intel i9-10900K under Node 24.21.0 at 1 to 11 % load from other work, on 22 October 2026.

A template’s draft is saved only from the version it was read at, its revision and its report’s digest: a save from a draft another author has saved over since is refused 412 draft-changed and writes nothing, so the host reads the draft again, and what its author changed meanwhile is the host’s to carry over.
Every saved revision of a draft stays in the store, and nothing prunes a revision or deletes a draft, a template or an image, so a tenant’s store only grows until an operator removes files by hand.

A revision is the number of a template’s newest file, so a backup restored from before the newest save, that file removed by hand, or its name lost on power loss has the next save issue the number again; a page still holding the draft that went is refused 412 draft-changed by its digest and reads the newest again, unless the draft saved again holds the same report to the byte, whose save goes through, and what the restore or the power loss took away is gone.

The digest a save names is compared with the newest draft’s just before the store’s swap, which is by revision alone, so where a draft’s newest file is removed by hand while the server runs and another save is given its number between one save’s comparison and its swap, that save can win over a draft its author never saw; the operator restores with the server stopped and never removes a draft’s newest file while it runs.
A replacing save reads the template’s newest draft once more just before the swap, and what that read costs has not been measured.

Each revision keeps the subject of the token that saved it, as savedBy, beside the tenant’s documents in the store and in every backup of its volume, so a host whose subjects are email addresses or an identity provider’s ids keeps them there at rest.
A stored draft’s digest covers its report and not its savedBy, so a record whose savedBy was edited by hand on the volume is served as edited, where one whose report was edited is refused.
A tenant’s directory in the store is the unkeyed SHA-256 of its tenant claim, so whoever can list the volume can tell which directory is a tenant whose claim they can guess.

A store an embedder writes for itself must keep absolute paths out of its errors: the server logs the file store’s own errors by fields that name no absolute path, and any other store’s error in its generic line as thrown, its message and stack included, which no test here exercises.
A draft that declares a font is refused asset-not-kept, since the server keeps no fonts, so a report mapped to a host’s fonts cannot be kept on the server in this release.

A report larger than report-spec’s MAX_REPORT_BYTES of JSON, the least power of two at least sixteen times the largest report the corpus held when it was measured, is refused 413 report-too-large as a draft however valid it is.

The server requires FORMANCY_REPORT_STORE_DIR, the absolute path of a directory that exists and that it can write, which the image sets: run outside the image it stops at start until the setting names one, and under docker run --read-only the directory must be a volume.
A save is decided by a hard link on the store’s volume, and nothing probes for one at start, so on a volume that cannot make one the server starts and answers every save internal.

A save is decided by a hard link, which is atomic on a local file system; on a volume over NFS a client can be told the wrong outcome of a save after a retransmission, and nothing here has run the store on one.
A saved revision’s file is flushed before it is linked, but its directory is not flushed after the link, as in Formancy Data’s store, so an acknowledged save can lose its name on power loss.

Listing a tenant’s templates reads every template’s newest draft, with no index, so its time grows with the templates, unmeasured, and one record that is not what the store wrote fails the whole list internal.

A malformed precondition, a body past its route’s limit and a media type the route does not read are answered before the actions table is asked, so a person without the capacity has a malformed save refused 400 rather than 403, and up to MAX_ASSET_BYTES of an image read before the 403.

A refusal answered before the body is read, the 401, a cross-origin 403 or a 415, closes the connection of a request that carries a body, so a client that keeps its connections alive opens a new one after each.

An SVG the server serves carries no X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and no sandboxing content security policy; the token its route needs and the drawing elements checkSvg admits alone stand in for them.

A host that previews a draft kept on the server writes its own image cache, reading every image the draft declares when it opens it and keeping each one a person adds, since the runtime’s resolver is synchronous and report-client has no helper.

report-client throws, before anything is sent, a token that is empty or no RFC 6750 bearer token, so a host that relied on the server’s 401 to send a signed-out person to sign in handles the throw instead.

report-client follows no redirect, as far as the fetch it is given honours redirect: error, so a server reached through one, a move from http: to https: on the same host among them, is a network error, and its base URL is the address the server answers at.

report-server-core depends on report-spec, so the server’s image ships report-spec and what it brings, @formancy/spec under Apache-2.0 among them, and a report-spec release is a release of the server.

The getting-started guide’s draft host is type-checked and bundled by the install gate and never run against a server, so its Save, its conflict and its reload rest on review and on report-client’s own suite.

An object written in place as a `ReportSession` whose `subscribe`, `document` or `hash` reads `this` no longer compiles, since those members are declared `this: void` for the store hooks that call them off the object; a class or a closure is unaffected.

An object written in place as a `ReportEditor` whose `subscribe` or `state` reads `this` no longer compiles, since those members are declared `this: void` for the store hooks that call them off the object; a class or a closure is unaffected.

The demo's headers are written by the deploy and measured by the browser gate under one function of the address, but nothing in this repository reads them from formancy.ai/report/, so a Cloudflare setting that drops or rewrites one goes unnoticed until somebody reads the response.

The browser gate hears what the demo's policy refuses in the page, and in Chromium alone: a refusal inside PDF.js's worker, or in Firefox or WebKit, is heard by nobody, though a worker that does not start fails the gate.
A chart reads the detail dataset alone, one field as its categories and each series a total of one field per category; a chart of an expression, of the header or of another dataset is not drawn.
A chart holds at most eight series, and a pie one series of a sum or a count.

A series is drawn in the palette’s colour at its place, and a pie’s slice in the colour at its category’s, so removing a series from the middle shifts the colour of every series after it, and no series keeps a colour of its own.
A report that holds a chart is refused whole by 0.2.0, which does not know the kind, so a report saved with one opens only in a release that has it.

Until the builders offer a chart and edit its own properties, neither palette has Chart, and a chart is written in the report’s JSON by a host or a proposal; a builder shows one a report holds, moves it and removes it.

A form version that removes the field a chart groups by is offered printing nothing of it only where the chart labels its rows without a category; a chart written without that label, over a field that may not be null, is offered the removal alone, which takes the chart.
The pages' browser gate runs in Chromium alone, as every browser gate here does, so a page's reflow, contrast, keyboard path and requests in Firefox or WebKit are measured by nobody.

The pages' browser gate serves the pages without the Studio beside them, so a link from a page to the Studio is never followed in a browser, and the demo as the deploy stages it is held by scripts/demo.test.mjs reading the files it stages, not opened.

The pages' browser gate asserts numbers and computed results and takes no screenshot, so nothing measures what a page looks like: a page laid out badly but within the window, legible and reached by the keyboard, passes.
A PDF that holds optional content is refused, even where every layer would print, as 116 of 1,484 PDFs that carry no person's data were when the reader was measured on 8 November 2026.

A PDF that is encrypted, cut short or damaged, whose cross-reference names an earlier definition of an object than the last one written, or that holds bytes between its objects is refused, never repaired.
A PDF past 20 MiB, 1,000 pages or 100,000 objects is refused, so a tagged report as dense as the densest measured is refused past about 700 pages and is to be added in parts.
A PDF that holds more than 2,000,000 values -- numbers, names, strings, arrays, dictionaries and references, its last trailer counted twice since it is read twice -- is refused.
The same count holds what each decoder a PDF's streams build costs, so a file of many short compressed streams or inline images is refused sooner than its values alone would be.
The same count holds three values for each annotation a PDF's pages list, every page together, so a thousand pages that share one list of more than about 660 annotations are refused.

A PDF with a stream behind a filter the reader does not decode where it must -- LZW, Crypt, a TIFF predictor, an image's own filter anywhere but last, or a name PDF does not define -- is refused, so an old file compressed with LZW is to be saved again.

A PDF that holds a form standing in for a page of another file (a reference XObject's /Ref), or an image or a form naming another file a printer may print in its place (/OPI), is refused, as one whose stream keeps its data in another file is, since Report fetches nothing by its address.

A PDF whose form is XFA or asks the viewer to draw its fields, or that holds an annotation that prints with no appearance, a link whose border a viewer would draw, or an annotation that stays upright on a turned page, is refused.

An inline image is refused wherever PDF.js 6.4.299 could end or begin its data otherwise than the reader does, which binary data holding `EI` and a white-space byte can do, and how many real files that refuses is not measured: none of the sample held an inline image.
Links, JavaScript, actions, attachments, form fields and signatures in a PDF are read as counts alone, never named, since a print of its pages keeps none of them.
`readDocument` takes a Uint8Array of the host's own realm and nothing else, so a host holding an ArrayBuffer, or an iframe's or a vm's array, copies it into a Uint8Array of its own first.

A read is synchronous and was measured within a second at its bounds on one laptop, files at several bounds at once among them, so a PDF at the bounds holds the thread it is read on for up to about a second there, and longer on battery or a slower machine.

pdf-lib and pako come with the reader into every bundle that reads a PDF, which added 234,035 bytes gzipped to the Studio's renderer chunk as measured of the spike's code that chose them, not measured again on the package.

What a read leaves in its process after it returns is not measured on this reader: it feeds pdf-lib's pools of names and references nothing of a file, which spies hold, and what those pools keep was measured on the spike's loop alone, so a long-running process that reads untrusted PDFs cannot yet rely on keeping nothing.

pdf-lib's stream decoders are ports of PDF.js's and XPDF's under Apache-2.0, which its dist and its MIT licence file do not say and the licence guard judges by pdf-lib's MIT field alone, so a bundle that holds the reader owes Apache-2.0's text and the ports' attribution, which only an entry of the Studio's embedded notices would carry and nothing fails without.
A chart of more than 200 categories, or a pie of more categories than its palette has colours -- eight unless it names its own -- is refused when it renders.
A pie refuses a negative value, and one whose values are all zero prints its empty text.
A chart's value axis is chosen by one rule, at most five steps of one, two or five times a power of ten; an author cannot set its range or its step.
A pie's shares are each rounded once, to a tenth of a percent, so they need not add up to 100.0 %: three equal slices print 33.3 % each.
A pie's legend entry that labels its value reads `label: value (share)`, its colon and its parentheses the same in every language.

A decimal category with no format prints as its first row in the data's order spells it, so a chart and a table sorted otherwise can spell one value differently, 7.7 and 7.70; a category format with a scale prints both alike.
A pie whose values its format cannot print is refused even where it labels none of them.

A release commit fails the pages' suite until the start page's status is written again beside the QR-bill and EPC QR code pages': what the release holds, said in the start page's hero, what Formancy Report does not do yet, what its totals do not do and that the report format is still a draft, each true of the release and of main, in four languages; and the release commit opens a new, empty Unreleased in CHANGELOG.md, whose heading the start page links, or the pages' link check refuses the site.

What the start page says Formancy Report does not do yet fails the pages' suite in the pull request that changes the code it rests on, but for one detail table grouped by one field at most; that sentence, the hero's standing and the totals' limits are read again only by a release commit, so between releases the start page at formancy.ai/report/, which is main's, can still say one of them after main has made it false. The other absences match packages by name and report-spec's lists, so a renderer, a viewer or a server published under another name passes them, and so do a barcode added as a property of an existing component kind and a new output format inside report-render-pdf.
The start page's topic cards, its exact totals and what it says Formancy Report does not do yet are no native speaker's words in French or Italian, and no review of them is recorded.

Every card on the product pages names the tests it rests on, each a test file or a gate's entry of the checkout, which the pages' suite holds; whether each still tests what its card says, whether a card's list holds every test its claim needs, and every sentence outside a card, the healthcare page's title, h1, description and lead among them, are held by review.

A word the product pages name as the Studio's, a starter's, the picker's or a button's, is held to the Studio's recorded pictures in docs/images/readme/captured.json, which the README pictures' check compares with the Studio's own text, and not to the Studio as it runs: the pages pass a starter renamed in the Studio until its pictures are taken again.
A PDF/A-2b, which a host asks for with `pdfa: '2b'`, is level b alone, so it has no structure tree and is no tagged, accessible PDF, and a receiver who asks for PDF/A-2a or 2u gets level b.

Whether a render is a PDF/A-2b is the host's choice at that render and no report says it, so a CMYK JPEG, an SVG whose box carries its numbers past what a PDF/A holds, or a title holding `&`, `<` or `>` is refused only by a render asked for as one, and neither the builders nor the validator warn of it beforehand.

A Factur-X e-invoice, an XRechnung's copy and a preview the runtime labels so are refused as `unsupported` when asked for as a PDF/A-2b, each to be rendered without `pdfa`, so a host that sets it on every render drops it for them.

A PDF/A-2b's render in Node reads PDFKit's ICC profile from `data/sRGB_IEC61966_2_1.icc` beside PDFKit's own code, as an e-invoice's does, so a host that bundles the Node entry ships that file where the bundled PDFKit's `__dirname` points, or every PDF/A-2b render fails with the file system's error, which nobody here has tried.

A preview that lacks nothing and is of no e-invoice carries no label, so it is drawn as a PDF/A-2b like its final render, which the renderer cannot tell it from and the tests show to be the same document for the quotation alone.

The starters that are no e-invoice, drawn as a PDF/A-2b, were 4,243 to 4,262 bytes larger than drawn plain, 25,037 to 77,558 bytes against 20,791 to 73,297, and the quotation's and grouped-equipment's medians of nine renders, the two timed, within 2 ms of the plain ones, within the noise of a machine at a load average about 6 from other work, measured on 11 November 2026 from the built packages on Node 22.23.3 and an Apple M2.

veraPDF judges as PDF/A-2b the starters that are no e-invoice, four variant pages on the quotation's, a page of charts among them, and the corpus's two fonts fixtures, so a customer's template is held by the renderer's refusals and not by a validator.

The e-invoice gate records every PDF/A-2b by the digest of its objects inflated, so a change to what a starter draws fails CI's `e-invoice` job and the judges' tests until somebody with a Java retakes the record with `--record` on a passing run.
A chart's category labels print across, never turned, wrapped or cut: a chart whose labels do not fit across is refused, to be widened or given shorter labels.
A chart's words take its style's font, size, weight, slant and colour; its alignment is not read.
A chart's grid, category axis, bar spacing, line weights, markers and legend swatches are the renderer's; only its colours and its words' style are the report's.

A bar chart whose bars would be narrower than 3.5 pt, the least the Studio's Preview draws apart at 100 % on a screen of device pixel ratio 2, is refused; at 75 %, or on a screen of ratio 1, the narrowest bars drawn may run together in the Preview, or in any reader that draws the PDF as coarsely, though the PDF keeps a gap between them.

A pie whose square would be narrower than 24.75 pt, the least at which the Studio's Preview shows a slice of one percent as its own colour at 100 % on a screen of device pixel ratio 2, is refused, whether its box or its title and legend leave it that little, so that a box of 72 pt with an 8-pt title and a legend holds a pie only where its legend is short; at 75 %, or on a screen of ratio 1, such a slice of the smallest pies drawn may run into its neighbours in the Preview, and a slice under one percent is thin at any size.
A chart that prints no word, and a keep-together block of an image alone, leave a heading kept with them at the foot of the page they leave when they move to the next.

A chart's categories, legend entries and title stay in the Node process or the page after its render, in zrender's width cache of up to 500 words for each of 100 fonts, which nothing zrender exports clears.
Every chart with something to draw is refused where a host's bundle gives ECharts another copy of zrender than the renderer's.

A preprocessor, processor, visual, layout or update a host registers on the ECharts it shares with the renderer -- the one copy a Node install or a bundler dedupes ECharts 6.1.0 to -- runs on the renderer's charts too, and changes their marks with nothing refused: a host's preprocessor that halves a bar series' data halves every bar the PDF prints, beside the runtime's words.

A render whose charts together weigh more than 5,000 units -- each chart its kind's weight (a bar 40, a line 60, a pie 10), a unit for each series at each category or each slice, and each word it places by what the word is (a title 6, a legend entry 5, a tick 2, a category or a value 1) -- is refused as `content-too-large` at the chart that crossed it, so a document of many dense charts, three line charts of 8 series and 200 categories or 50 titled line charts of one series and twelve months among them, is split across renders.

The chart bound was measured on one Apple M2, the weights on the render and on PDF.js at scale 1 at a load average of 12 to 20, a line's, a title's and a tick's again at 3.0 to 3.2, each word's the larger of the two runs', and the bound by the slowest of seven runs of the forms tried at 3.3 to 5.6, where the slowest render of them took 878 ms and the slowest page 1,614 ms, a second run at 4.2 to 5.5 found two others slowest, at 1,258 and 1,255 ms, and a third, once a line weighed 60, at 3.0 to 3.9, 1,202 ms in one spike; nothing measured the slowest the bound admits, and at a load of 10 to 18.6 documents it admitted took up to 9.45 s.

A heading kept with the next block makes pdfmake lay the whole document out again for each page it moves a heading to, charts and all, which the chart bound does not count: 17 bar charts the bound admits took two and a half times as long behind kept headings as behind plain ones.

A chart's paint counts against no SVG budget: one line chart of 8 series and 200 categories, as wide as an A4 landscape page and a third of its height, weighs nearly four times the segments the body's SVG images may cost together, and the chart bound admits two of them on a page.

Installing the renderer installs Apache ECharts 6.1.0 and zrender 6.1.0, 62,176 KiB and 5,168 KiB by `du -sk` on 15 November 2026, for a host that never draws a chart too; a browser loads the chart chunk, 189.00 kB gzipped by the Studio's build on that day, only with the first document that holds a chart with marks.

The renderer depends on Apache ECharts under Apache-2.0, whose NOTICE a host that bundles it carries, with d3's BSD-3-Clause for the code ECharts took from it, zrender under BSD-3-Clause and tslib under 0BSD.

A chart is proved on its PDF by its clip, its paths and its words, so an empty chart's box, a pie's arc up to about half a point off its circle, a chart beside an SVG image of its very size but by their order, document order where columns break across pages, a label in a face whose metrics stand apart from the three its tolerance was measured on, a colour a reader cannot tell from its neighbour and a mark under a word are not seen.

A group header that states how many of its rows it is kept with moves to the next page with them where fewer would fit at the foot of one, leaving that room blank, so a report that states a count can need more pages than without, and is refused as too-many-pages where that passes the host's limit, once it is measured whole.

A group header's count is a most: where its stated rows do not fit on a page under the table's repeated column header, it is kept with as many as fit, or with its first row alone, and nothing says that fewer were kept.
A count of one and no count print alike and hash differently: the builders write the absence, and a host or a proposal may write either.
A group header is kept with at most 32 of its rows, MAX_KEEP_WITH_ROWS, a bound chosen, not measured.
A row with no text ends no count: a group header whose last stated rows print nothing is kept with the rows before them that do, and those that print nothing may stand on the next page.

A group no longer than its count whose footer row or total after its subtotal prints nothing is kept whole with that blank row, and, where the table's breaks are planned, in the body outside a frame, moves whole to the next page where the blank row would not fit with it.

A group header that prints nothing is kept with no more than its first row, whatever its count: a table's first group header still moves with that row under the column header, and any other is left where it falls.
The builders show a group's count of kept rows on its table's properties though the group's header has no text, where the renderer keeps no more than the header's first row with it.
In a table whose rows may split across pages, the last row a group header keeps starts on the header's page and may continue on the next.

A report that states a count is refused whole by 0.2.0 as an unknown property, and a 0.2.0 renderer handed a document this release's runtime resolved keeps each group header with its first row alone, reading no member of a row it does not know.

The corpus's fixture for kept rows is built of rows that fit, so a header kept with fewer rows than its count, where they do not, is proved by the renderer's own cases alone, each stating the count it expects from the heights it computes.

A page number or a page count is refused in page 1's own header, since it is drawn before the pages are counted: page 1's number and count print in the page footer, and a first page header copied from a page header that numbers its pages is refused until the number is taken out.

No header on page 1 is written as an empty header of page 1's own, which the format has no other word for: a person who chooses a header of page 1's own and adds nothing to it gets no header on page 1.

`REGION_NAMES` lists six regions and a report may hold five of them, so an integrator who iterates the list meets `firstPageHeader` missing from a report without one; report-spec's `heldRegions` lists the regions a report holds.
Choosing the page header again for page 1 in either builder's report properties removes page 1's own header with everything it holds, in one step that undo brings back.

In a report with a header of page 1's own, an image, a QR code or another block of fixed height taller than the shorter of page 1's body and the later pages' bodies is refused, though a later page could hold it.

Where page 1's own header takes more room than the page header, a block kept together, or a table's first rows kept with its column header, that page 1's body cannot hold starts page 2, and page 1 prints its header with nothing under it.

Where page 1's own header takes less room than the page header, a kept block, a table's line under its repeated header or an image that only page 1's taller body could hold is refused, even in a report that would end on page 1.

A header of page 1's own that reaches into a QR-bill's slip is refused, though the report runs on to a later page whose page header leaves the slip its room, since which page is the last is known only once the pages are laid out.
The page header of a report with a header of page 1's own is measured and held to leaving the later pages' body room, even where the report has one page and no page prints it.

A report that holds a first page header is refused whole by 0.2.0 as an unknown property, so a report saved with one opens only in a release that has the region; and a 0.2.0 renderer handed a document this runtime resolved prints the page header on page 1 without a word, so the runtime and the renderer must be of one release.

A run is set below or above the line only in a text component’s paragraph: a table’s column value, group header and footer cells and totals, and what a QR code, an EPC QR code, a QR-bill or an e-invoice encodes refuse a `baseline` as `misplaced-baseline`, and a page number or count as `unknown-property`, so a unit’s power in a cell is printed as Unicode’s raised form where the face maps it, or not at all.

No text format lowers a formula’s digits read from a field, so C6H12O6 from the data prints on the line unless the data carries Unicode’s lowered digits, U+2080 to U+2089, which Roboto and Liberation Serif both map.

A report that sets a run below or above the line is refused whole by 0.2.0 as `unknown-property`, so a report saved with one opens only in a release that has the property, and a host that maps every one of report-spec’s error codes to its own message meets `misplaced-baseline`, which it has none for.

A run set below or above the line prints at pdfmake’s one size and move, 58 % of its paragraph’s size, raised 43.5 % of the size or lowered 20.3 %; a face’s own superscript and subscript metrics are not read, and a run cannot be set smaller, larger, higher or lower.
